grid.statement: NLGEOM,ON activates large-deflection effects; select Large Displacement Static when large deflections are expected (e.g. a long, slender bar under bending)
LNSRCH activates the line search option (listed in the Nonlinear tab options of Solution Controls)
PRED activates a predictor on the degree-of-freedom solution; NEQIT specifies the maximum number of equilibrium iterations allowed per substep
CNVTOL sets the convergence criteria; CUTCONTROL controls bisections (cutback criteria)

NROPT (Newton-Raphson option) is used only in a nonlinear analysis and specifies how often the tangent matrix is updated: Program-chosen (default), Full, Modified, Initial stiffness, Full with unsymmetric matrix
AUTOTS enables automatic time stepping; DELTIM and NSUBST control the time step size / number of substeps (TIME sets time at end of load step)

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,OFF ignores large-deflection effects (a small-deflection analysis is specified); this option is the default.
dFacts.note: Lines 52003-52005: 'OFF / Ignores large-deflection effects (that is, a small-deflection analysis is specified). This option is the default.' Cited line is within the statement span.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON includes large-deflection (large rotation) effects or large strain effects, according to the element type.
dFacts.note: Lines 52006-52008: 'ON / Includes large-deflection (large rotation) effects or large strain effects, according to the element type.' Adds large-strain/element-type detail beyond G1, so not a duplicate.

dFacts.statement: When large-deflection effects are included (NLGEOM,ON), stress stiffening effects are also included automatically, and the command is valid only within the first load step during the solution.
dFacts.note: Lines 52014-52016: stress stiffening included automatically when NLGEOM,ON (52014-52015); 'If used during the solution (/SOLU), this command is valid only within the first load step.' (52016). Cited line is in-span.

dFacts.statement: In a large-deflection analysis, pressure loads behave differently than other load types.
dFacts.note: Line 52017 verbatim: 'In a large-deflection analysis, pressure loads behave differently than other load types.'

dFacts.statement: AUTOTS,OFF means do not use automatic time stepping; AUTOTS,ON means use automatic time stepping (default).
dFacts.note: Lines 9988-9992: 'Automatic time stepping key: / OFF / Do not use automatic time stepping. / ON / Use automatic time stepping (default).' Cited line is the key label header immediately above the supporting text. Overlaps G6 (ON meaning) but adds the OFF clause, so kept.

dFacts.statement: AUTOTS Command Default: automatic time stepping is on by default.
dFacts.note: Line 9996 verbatim (under 'Command Default', line 9995): 'Automatic time stepping is on by default.'

dFacts.statement: AUTOTS,ON uses both time step prediction and time step bisection.
dFacts.note: Cited line 9998 is a copyright/page line. True support at lines 10003-10004 (Notes): 'If Key = ON, both time step prediction and time step bisection will be used.'

dFacts.statement: Automatic time stepping (AUTOTS), line search (LNSRCH), and the DOF predictor (PRED) cannot be used with the arc-length method (ARCLEN, ARCTRM); if used, the program disables these settings.
dFacts.note: Lines 10007-10012: 'You cannot use automatic time stepping (AUTOTS), line search (LNSRCH), or the DOF solution predictor (PRED) with the arc-length method (ARCLEN, ARCTRM)... the program disables your automatic time stepping, line search, and DOF predictor settings...' Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: LNSRCH activates a line search to be used with Newton-Raphson; LNSRCH,ON suppresses adaptive descent unless explicitly requested on NROPT, and having both on at the same time is not recommended.
dFacts.note: Line 45414 verbatim: 'Activates a line search to be used with Newton-Raphson.'; lines 45422-45424: adaptive descent suppressed when LNSRCH on unless requested on NROPT, both on not recommended. Extends G2 with new content, so kept.

dFacts.statement: LNSRCH,AUTO has the program automatically switch line searching ON and OFF between substeps of a load step as needed (recommended).
dFacts.note: Lines 45425-45427: 'AUTO / The program automatically switches line searching ON and OFF between substeps of a load step as needed. This option is recommended.' Cited line is the option token.

dFacts.statement: LNSRCH LSTOL is the line search convergence tolerance (default = 0.5); LStrun default is OFF meaning no truncation.
dFacts.note: Lines 45433-45437: 'LSTOL / Line search convergence tolerance (default = 0.5).' and 'LStrun ... Default = OFF, meaning no truncation.' Cited line is the LSTOL token.

dFacts.statement: LNSRCH Command Default: line search off, unless contact elements are present.
dFacts.note: Lines 45439-45440: 'Command Default / Line search off, unless contact elements are present.' Cited line is the section header.

dFacts.statement: NROPT,AUTO lets the program choose the option (default); NROPT,FULL uses full Newton-Raphson.
dFacts.note: Line 53389-53393 verified ('AUTO Let the program choose the option (default). / FULL Use full Newton-Raphson.') but the claim is already in G5, which lists the NROPT options 'Program-chosen (default), Full, ...'. No new content beyond keyword spelling.

dFacts.statement: NROPT,MODI uses modified Newton-Raphson; NROPT,INIT uses the previously computed (initial-stiffness) matrix.
dFacts.note: Lines 53399-53402 verified ('MODI Use modified Newton-Raphson. / INIT Use the previously computed matrix (initial-stiffness).') but G5 already lists the 'Modified' and 'Initial stiffness' options. No new content beyond keyword spelling.

dFacts.statement: NROPT,UNSYM uses full Newton-Raphson with unsymmetric matrices of elements where the unsymmetric option exists.
dFacts.note: True text at lines 53403-53405 (cited 53402 is the INIT line) but the claim matches G5's listed option 'Full with unsymmetric matrix'. No material new content.

dFacts.statement: NROPT adaptive descent: ON uses adaptive descent (default if frictional contact exists; explicit ON valid only if Option=FULL); OFF does not use adaptive descent (default in all other cases).
dFacts.note: Cited line 53409 is the Option2=CRPL creep line. True support at lines 53413-53417: 'ON / Use adaptive descent (default if frictional contact exists). Explicit ON is valid only if Option = FULL. / OFF / Do not use adaptive descent (default in all other cases).'

dFacts.statement: NROPT,MODI and NROPT,INIT are only applicable with the sparse solver (EQSLV,SPARSE); thermal analyses always use full Newton-Raphson.
dFacts.note: Cited line 53431 is a copyright line. True support at lines 53439-53441: 'NROPT,MODI and NROPT,INIT are only applicable with the sparse solver (EQSLV,SPARSE). Thermal analyses will always use full Newton-Raphson irrespective of the Option1 value selected.'

dFacts.statement: NEQIT specifies the maximum number of equilibrium iterations for nonlinear analyses.
dFacts.note: Line 51241 verified verbatim, but G3 already states 'NEQIT specifies the maximum number of equilibrium iterations allowed per substep'. Same claim, no new content.

dFacts.statement: NEQIT Command Default: the maximum number of equilibrium iterations per substep is set between 15 and 26, depending on the physics of the problem.
dFacts.note: Cited line 51254 is the tail of the FORCEkey note. True support at lines 51255-51257: 'Command Default / The maximum number of equilibrium iterations per substep is set between 15 and 26, depending on the physics of the problem.'

dFacts.statement: CNVTOL sets convergence values for nonlinear analyses.
dFacts.note: Line 17608 verified verbatim ('Sets convergence values for nonlinear analyses.'), but G4 already states 'CNVTOL sets the convergence criteria'. Same claim, no new content.

dFacts.statement: CNVTOL force convergence labels include F (Forces), M (Moments), DVOL (Volume), HDSP (Hydrostatic Pressure), ENGY (Energy Error); displacement labels include U (Displacements), ROT (Rotations), JOINT, COMP.
dFacts.note: Label table at lines 17613-17640 lists Forces/F, Moments/M, Volume/DVOL, Hydrostatic Pressure/HDSP, Energy Error/ENGY, Displacements/U, Rotations/ROT, JOINT, COMP. Cited line 17616 is the table header directly above the content.

dFacts.statement: CNVTOL VALUE defaults to the maximum of a program-calculated reference or MINREF; if VALUE is negative, the convergence criterion for that label is removed.
dFacts.note: Cited line 17709 is inside footnote [c] (ENGY). True support at lines 17716-17721: 'VALUE defaults to the maximum of a program calculated reference or MINREF... If VALUE is negative, the convergence criterion based on the specified label is removed...'

dFacts.statement: CNVTOL default TOLER when CNVTOL issued with Lab but no TOLER: 0.05 (5%) for displacement (U), 0.05 for energy error (ENGY), 0.005 (0.5%) for all other labels.
dFacts.note: Cited line 17719 is the VALUE-negative sentence. True support at lines 17724-17733: 'If CNVTOL is issued with a Lab value specified but no TOLER value, the default tolerance values are: 0.05 (5%) for displacement (U)... 0.05 for energy error (ENGY)... For all other Lab labels, the default tolerance value is 0.005 (0.5%).'

dFacts.statement: If CNVTOL is not issued, TOLER defaults are 0.005 (0.5%) for force (F) and moment (M), 1.0E-4 (0.01%) for volume (DVOL), 0.05 (5%) for displacement (U).
dFacts.note: Cited line 17726 is a bullet of the previous list. True support at lines 17734-17737: 'If CNVTOL is not issued, the TOLER defaults are as follows: 0.005 (0.5%) for force (F) and moment (M) / 1.0E-4 (0.01%) for volume (DVOL) / 0.05 (5%) for displacement (U).'

dFacts.statement: CNVTOL NORM: 0 = Infinite norm (default for Lab=U); 1 = L1 norm; 2 = L2 norm (check SRSS value, default except Lab=U); 3 = Infinite norm based on current displacement increment (Lab=U only).
dFacts.note: Cited line 17745 is a THOPT continuation line. True support at lines 17752-17765 (NORM): 0 Infinite norm (default for Lab=U), 1 L1 norm, 2 L2 norm (check SRSS value) (default, except for Lab=U), 3 Infinite norm based on displacement increment of the substep (Valid only for Lab=U).

dFacts.statement: CNVTOL MINREF default is the maximum of 0.01 or the internally calculated minimum reference value for force (F), moment (M).
dFacts.note: Cited line 17762 is the NORM=2 (L2 norm) line. True support at lines 17766-17770 (MINREF): 'maximum of 0.01 or internally calculated minimum reference value for force (F), moment (M).'

dFacts.statement: CUTCONTROL controls time-step cutback during a nonlinear solution.
dFacts.note: Line 19446 verified verbatim ('Controls time-step cutback during a nonlinear solution.'), but G4 already states 'CUTCONTROL controls bisections (cutback criteria)'. Same claim, no new content.

dFacts.statement: CUTCONTROL PLSLIMIT is the maximum equivalent plastic strain allowed within a time-step; default Value = 0.15 (15 percent).
dFacts.note: Cited line 19508 is the tail of the MDMG entry. True support at lines 19509-19512: 'PLSLIMIT / Maximum equivalent plastic strain allowed within a time-step (substep)... Default: Value = 0.15 (15 percent).'

dFacts.statement: CUTCONTROL CUTBACKFACTOR default is 0.5 (if Value not specified), and it is valid only when automatic time stepping is on (AUTOTS,ON).
dFacts.note: Cited line 19466 is the tail of the CRPLIMIT entry. True support at lines 19469-19473: 'CUTBACKFACTOR ... 0 < Value < 1 (default is 0.5 if Value is not specified.) The option to change the cutback factor is valid only when automatic time stepping is on (AUTOTS,ON), which is the default.'

dFacts.statement: CUTCONTROL ROTLIMIT default Value = 1.0 x 10^7 for the maximum rotation DOF increment.
dFacts.note: Cited line 19537 is the TEMPLIMIT entry. True support at lines 19531-19535: 'ROTLIMIT / Set the maximum rotation degree-of-freedom increment allowed within a time step... If not specified, default Value = 1.0 x 107.' ('107' = 10^7 superscript rendering).

dFacts.statement: DELTIM specifies the time step sizes for the current load step; DTIME is the time step size, and with AUTOTS it is the starting time substep.
dFacts.note: Line 22056 verbatim: 'Specifies the time step sizes to be used for the current load step.'; lines 22060-22061: 'DTIME ... Time step size for this step. If automatic time stepping is used (AUTOTS), DTIME is the starting time substep.'

dFacts.statement: NSUBST specifies the number of substeps to be taken this load step; NSBSTP with AUTOTS defines the size of the first substep.
dFacts.note: Line 54698 verbatim; line 54703: 'If automatic time stepping is used (AUTOTS), NSBSTP defines the size of the first substep.'

dFacts.statement: NSUBST NSBMX is the maximum number of substeps (minimum time step size) and NSBMN is the minimum number of substeps (maximum time step size) if automatic time stepping is used.
dFacts.note: Cited line 54705 is the NSBSTP default text. True support at lines 54707-54710 (NSBMX: 'Maximum number of substeps to be taken (that is, the minimum time step size) if automatic time stepping is used') and 54716-54719 (NSBMN: 'Minimum number of substeps... maximum time step size').

dFacts.statement: NSUBST Carry = ON uses the final time step from the previous load step as the starting time step (if automatic time stepping is used).
dFacts.note: Cited line 54717 is the NSBMN description. True support at lines 54724-54726: 'ON / Use final time step from previous load step as the starting time step (if automatic time stepping is used).'

dFacts.statement: It is recommended that all fields of NSUBST be specified, and changing the number of substeps upon restarting an analysis during a load step is not recommended.
dFacts.note: Cited line 54727 is a generic default sentence. True support at lines 54729-54730 ('It is recommended that all fields of this command be specified for solution efficiency and robustness') and 54733 ('Changing the number of substeps upon restarting an analysis during a load step is not recommended').

dFacts.statement: PRED activates a predictor in a nonlinear analysis; PRED,AUTO (default) has the program use a predictor but automatically switch prediction off within certain exceptions.
dFacts.note: Line 63009 verbatim; lines 63014-63016: 'AUTO / The program uses a predictor but, within certain exceptions, automatically switches prediction off. This behavior is the default'. Adds the AUTO-default detail beyond G3's PRED clause, so kept.

dFacts.statement: PRED,LINERAR (or ON) uses the linear predictor on all substeps after the first; PRED,QUADRATIC uses the quadratic predictor on all substeps after the second.
dFacts.note: Cited line 63018 is the OFF ('No prediction occurs') entry. True support at lines 63019-63022: 'LINEAR (or ON) / Use the linear predictor on all substeps after the first. / QUADRATIC / Use the quadratic predictor on all substeps after the second.'

dFacts.statement: NCNV KSTOP: 0 = do not terminate the analysis if the solution fails to converge; 1 = terminate the analysis and program execution (default); 2 = terminate the analysis but not program execution.
dFacts.note: Lines 51115-51121: 'KSTOP / Program behavior upon nonconvergence: 0 Do not terminate... / 1 Terminate the analysis and the program execution... (default) / 2 Terminate the analysis, but not the program execution...'. Cited line is the KSTOP label header.

dFacts.statement: NCNV DLIM terminates program execution if the largest nodal DOF solution value exceeds the limit, defaulting to 1.0E6 (except MAG/A); ITLIM defaults to infinity.
dFacts.note: Lines 51128-51133: DLIM 'Terminates program execution if the largest nodal DOF solution value... exceeds this limit. Defaults to 1.0E6 for all DOF except MAG and A'; ITLIM '(defaults to infinity)'. Cited line is in-span.

dFacts.statement: STABILIZE activates stabilization for all elements that support nonlinear stabilization; Key OFF is default, CONSTANT keeps the energy-dissipation ratio/damping factor constant, REDUCE reduces it linearly to zero at the end of the load step.
dFacts.note: Line 79353 verbatim; lines 79358-79365: OFF 'Deactivate stabilization (default)'; CONSTANT 'remains constant during the load step'; REDUCE 'reduced linearly to zero at the end of the load step'.

dFacts.statement: STABILIZE Method ENERGY (default) uses the energy-dissipation ratio as the control; DAMPING uses the damping factor as the control.
dFacts.note: Cited line 79369 is a page header ('STABILIZE'). True support at lines 79371-79376: 'Method / ENERGY / Use the energy-dissipation ratio as the control. This value is the default when Key <> OFF. / DAMPING / Use the damping factor as the control.'

dFacts.statement: STABILIZE FORCELIMIT is the stabilization force limit coefficient, 0 < FORCELIMIT < 1, default value 0.2.
dFacts.note: Cited line 79385 is the SubStpOpt=NO text. True support at lines 79392-79394: 'FORCELIMIT / The stabilization force limit coefficient, such that 0 < FORCELIMIT < 1. The default value is 0.2.'

dFacts.statement: ARCLEN activates the arc-length method; MAXARC default = 25, MINARC default = 1/1000.
dFacts.note: Lines 8822-8835: 'ARCLEN,Key,MAXARC,MINARC / Activates the arc-length method... MAXARC Maximum multiplier of the reference arc-length radius (default = 25). MINARC Minimum multiplier... (default = 1/1000).' Cited line is verbatim the activation sentence.

dFacts.statement: The initial arc-length load factor is given by Initial Load Factor = TIME / NSBSTP.
dFacts.note: Cited line 8838 is the preceding sentence. True support at lines 8839-8841: 'The initial arc-length radius, t0, is proportional... to the initial load factor. The initial load factor is given by: Initial Load Factor = TIME / NSBSTP'.

dFacts.statement: The arc-length method ignores AUTOTS and PRED, and also ignores STABILIZE and LNSRCH.
dFacts.note: Cited line 8852 is 'tMIN = MINARC * t0'. True support at lines 8859-8861: '...the AUTOTS and PRED commands are ignored when the arc-length method is used. The STABILIZE and LNSRCH commands are also ignored.'

dFacts.statement: OUTPR controls the solution printout; Freq prints the solution for this item every Freqth (and the last) substep, ALL prints every substep, LAST prints only the last substep.
dFacts.note: Lines 56505-56509: 'Print solution for this item every Freqth (and the last) substep... If ALL, print solution for this item for every substep. If LAST, print solution for this item only for the last substep'; Notes 56524 'Controls the solution items to be printed...'. Cited line is in-span.

dFacts.statement: OUTRES controls the solution-result data written to the database.
dFacts.note: Line 56597 verbatim: 'Controls the solution-result data written to the database.'

dFacts.statement: RESCONTROL controls file writing for multiframe restarts; DEFINE specifies how often .xnnn restart files are written for a load step.
dFacts.note: Line 68168 verbatim; lines 68173-68176: 'DEFINE / Specifies how often .xnnn restart files (default)... are written for a load step.'

dFacts.statement: The procedure for a nonlinear static analysis includes Building the Model, Setting Solution Controls, Applying Loads, Solving the Analysis, Reviewing the Results, Terminating and Restarting, and uses traditional forward solving but can also be applied to inverse solving.
dFacts.note: Lines 13810-13823: task list 8.6.1 Building the Model ... 8.6.7 Terminating and Restarting a Running Job, and line 13823 verbatim: 'The procedure uses traditional forward solving but can also be applied to inverse solving (p. 290).' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: When setting ANTYPE and NLGEOM, select Large Displacement Static if you expect large deflections (long slender bar under bending) or large strains (metal-forming problem).
dFacts.note: Lines 1614-1617 verbatim including 'Select Large Displacement Static if you expect large deflections (as in the case of a long, slender bar under bending) or large strains (as in a metal-forming problem)'. Cited line in-span. Partially overlaps G1 but adds the large-strain selection criterion, so kept.

dFacts.statement: When setting ANTYPE and NLGEOM in a nonlinear static analysis, choose Large Displacement Static for a new analysis; you cannot change this setting after the first load step (after the first SOLVE command).
dFacts.note: Lines 13846-13850: 'When setting ANTYPE and NLGEOM, choose Large Displacement Static if you are performing a new analysis... You cannot change this setting after the first load step (that is, after issuing the first SOLVE command)'. Cited line in-span; the cannot-change clause is new vs G1.

dFacts.statement: The NSUBST and DELTIM commands achieve the same effect (starting, minimum, and maximum step size) by reciprocal means; if automatic time-stepping is off (AUTOTS), the starting substep size is used throughout the load step.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13855 is a copyright line. True support at lines 13860-13864: 'The NSUBST and DELTIM commands both achieve the same effect (establishing a load step's starting, minimum, and maximum step size), but by reciprocal means... If automatic time-stepping is off (AUTOTS), then the starting substep size is used throughout the load step.'

dFacts.statement: The OUTRES command controls data on the results file (Jobname.rst); by default only the last substep is written in a nonlinear analysis.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13859 is unrelated substep text. True support at lines 13865-13866: 'The OUTRES command controls the data on the results file (Jobname.rst). By default, only the last substep is written to the results file in a nonlinear analysis.'

dFacts.statement: Automatic solution control activates the sparse direct solver (EQSLV,SPARSE) for most cases, and it is recommended for beam/shell structures and ill-conditioned problems with insufficient displacement constraints.
dFacts.note: Line 13871 verbatim; recommendations at 13882 ('If it is a beam/shell... use the sparse direct solver') and 13885-13887 ('If the problem is ill-conditioned... or has insufficient displacement boundary constraints, use the sparse direct solver'), all within +30 of the cited line.

dFacts.statement: Automatic solution control enables automatic time-stepping (AUTOTS,ON), predicting the next time-step size based on number of equilibrium iterations, nonlinear element status change predictions, plastic strain increment, and creep strain increment.
dFacts.note: Lines 13892-13906: 'Automatic solution control enables automatic time-stepping (AUTOTS,ON)... the size of the next time step is predicted based on these factors: Number of equilibrium iterations... Predictions for nonlinear element status change... Size of the plastic strain increment... Size of the creep strain increment.' Cited line verbatim the anchor.

dFacts.statement: The automatic solution convergence check uses the L2-norm of force (and moment) with TOLER equal to 0.5%, and in most cases an infinite norm check on displacement with TOLER 5% is also used as a double-check.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13911 is the preceding sentence. True support at lines 13912-13916: 'The automatic solution convergence check uses the L2-norm of force (and moment) with a tolerance (TOLER) equal to 0.5%... an infinite norm check on displacement with TOLER equal to 5% is also used... serves as a double-check on convergence.'

dFacts.statement: By default, the program checks force convergence by comparing the SRSS of the force imbalances against VALUE*TOLER, where VALUE defaults to the SRSS of applied loads or MINREF (which defaults to 0.01), whichever is greater.
dFacts.note: Lines 13917-13920 verbatim (SRSS of force imbalances against VALUE*TOLER; VALUE default SRSS of applied loads or MINREF (defaults to 0.01), whichever is greater). Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: You should continue to use the default value of VALUE, changing convergence criteria by adjusting TOLER not VALUE, and ensure the default MINREF = 0.01 makes sense.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13928 is the preceding sentence. True support at lines 13930-13932: 'you should continue to use the default value of VALUE; that is, change the convergence criteria by adjusting TOLER, not VALUE. You should make certain that the default value of MINREF = 0.01 makes sense in the context of your analysis.'

dFacts.statement: The infinite norm repeats the single-DOF check at each DOF; the L1 norm compares against the sum of absolute values; the L2 norm uses SRSS; normally convergence in one norm implies convergence in the others.
dFacts.note: Lines 13937-13950: infinite norm 13937-13938, L1 norm 13944-13945, L2 norm (SRSS) 13946-13947, 'Normally, if an analysis converges in one norm, it will converge in the other norms' 13949-13950. Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: Automatic solution control sets NEQIT to between 15 and 26 iterations; if convergence is not satisfied within this number and auto time-stepping is on, the program attempts to bisect, or terminates/moves on according to NCNV.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13944 is the L1-norm bullet. True support at lines 13952-13959: 'Automatic solution control sets the value of NEQIT to between 15 and 26 iterations... the program attempts to bisect. If bisection is not possible, then the analysis either terminates or moves on to the next load step (according to NCNV command settings).'

dFacts.statement: Automatic solution control activates a predictor (PRED,ON); the linear extrapolation is based on the previous time step's accumulated displacement increment, the quadratic on the previous two, and quadratic predicts better for rotational DOFs (ROTX, ROTY, ROTZ).
dFacts.note: Lines 13961-13974: 'Automatic solution control activates a predicator (PRED,ON)' (13961); linear extrapolation on previous time step's accumulated displacement increment, quadratic on previous + prior-to-previous (13966-13970); 'quadratic extrapolation typically predicts better... for solutions with rotational degrees of freedom (ROTX, ROTY, ROTZ)' (13972-13974). Cited line is inside the supporting span.

dFacts.statement: Automatic solution control toggles line search on and off as needed: LNSRCH is toggled on for most contact problems and off for most non-contact problems.
dFacts.note: Lines 13979-13980 verbatim: 'Automatic solution control toggles line search on and off as needed. For most contact problems, LNSRCH is toggled on. For most non-contact problems, LNSRCH is toggled off.'

dFacts.statement: The line search multiplies the calculated displacement increment by a scale factor between 0 and 1 when stiffening is detected; it is an alternative to adaptive descent (NROPT), and activating both simultaneously is not recommended.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13983 is a copyright page-break line inside the paragraph. True support at lines 13981-13990: 'multiplies the calculated displacement increment by a program-calculated scale factor (having a value between 0 and 1), whenever a stiffening response is detected... alternative to the adaptive descent option (NROPT)... We do not recommend activating both line search and adaptive descent simultaneously.'

dFacts.statement: When an imposed displacement exists, a run cannot converge until at least one iteration has a line search value of 1, and the program does not impose the full displacement until then.
dFacts.note: Lines 13991-13995 verbatim: 'When an imposed displacement exists, a run cannot converge until at least one of the iterations has a line search value of 1... Until one of the iterations has a line search value of 1, the program does not impose the full value of the displacement.'

dFacts.statement: CUTCONTROL provides finer control over bisections and cutback in time-step size; by default for Lab=PLSLIMIT, Value is set to 15 percent.
dFacts.note: Lines 13997-13999: 'For finer control over bisections and cutback in time-step size, use (CUTCONTROL, Lab, Value, Option). By default, for Lab = PLSLIMIT (maximum plastic strain increment limit), Value is set to 15 percent.' Cited line in-span; adds the 15% default beyond G4.

dFacts.statement: Automatic solution control uses the FULL Newton-Raphson option (NROPT) with adaptive descent off if a nonlinearity is present, but turns adaptive descent on automatically for node-to-node/node-to-surface contact with friction.
dFacts.note: Lines 14023-14031: 'Automatic solution control uses the FULL Newton-Raphson option (NROPT) with adaptive descent off if there is a nonlinearity present. However, when node-to-node, node-to-surface contact elements are used for contact analysis with friction, then adaptive descent is automatically turned on.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: NROPT,FULL updates the stiffness matrix at every equilibrium iteration; with adaptive descent on, the program discards divergent iterations and restarts using a weighted combination of secant and tangent matrices.
dFacts.note: Lines 14036-14044: 'Full (NROPT,FULL): The program uses the full Newton-Raphson procedure, in which the stiffness matrix is updated at every equilibrium iteration... If divergent trends are detected on an iteration, the program discards the divergent iteration and restarts the solution, using a weighted combination of the secant and tangent stiffness matrices.' Cited line is the anchor bullet.

dFacts.statement: NROPT,MODI updates the tangent stiffness matrix at each substep and is not applicable to large-deformation analyses; NROPT,INIT uses the initial stiffness matrix and is also not applicable to large-deformation analyses.
dFacts.note: Lines 14049-14057: MODI 'tangent stiffness matrix is updated at each substep... not applicable to large-deformation analyses'; INIT 'uses the initial stiffness matrix in every equilibrium iteration... not applicable to large-deformation analyses'. Cited line is the anchor bullet; adds not-applicable-to-large-deformation detail beyond G5.

dFacts.statement: You should first try NROPT,FULL, then try NROPT,UNSYM if you experience convergence difficulties; a multistatus element is updated at the iteration in which it changes status irrespective of the Newton-Raphson option.
dFacts.note: Cited line 14070 is a copyright line. True support at lines 14075-14079: 'You should first try NROPT,FULL, then try NROPT,UNSYM if you experience convergence difficulties... If a multistatus element is in the model, it is updated at the iteration in which it changes status, irrespective of the Newton-Raphson option.'

dFacts.statement: To account for buckling/bifurcation behavior, the program includes stress stiffness in all geometrically nonlinear analyses (NLGEOM,ON).
dFacts.note: Lines 14020-14021 verbatim: 'To account for buckling, bifurcation behavior, the program includes stress stiffness in all geometrically nonlinear analyses (NLGEOM,ON).'

dFacts.statement: Bisection provides a means of automatically recovering from a convergence failure by cutting a time-step size in half when equilibrium iterations fail to converge and restarting from the last converged substep.
dFacts.note: Lines 12984-12986 verbatim: 'Bisection provides a means of automatically recovering from a convergence failure. This feature cuts a time-step size in half whenever equilibrium iterations fail to converge and automatically restart from the last converged substep.'

dFacts.statement: In a large-deflection analysis, nodal coordinate system orientations are not updated and calculated displacements are output in the original directions; pressure loads always act normal to the deflected element surface.
dFacts.note: Lines 13003-13004: 'Nodal coordinate system orientations are not updated in a large deflection analysis. Calculated displacements are therefore output in the original directions.'; lines 12999-13000: 'Pressure loads always act normal to the deflected element surface'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: Large-strain analyses account for stiffness changes from changes in an element's shape and orientation; NLGEOM,ON activates large-strain effects and the procedure places no theoretical limit on total rotation or strain.
dFacts.note: Lines 13046-13047: 'large-strain analyses account for the stiffness changes that result from changes in an element's shape and orientation. NLGEOM,ON... activates large-strain effects...'; lines 13050-13051: 'The large-strain procedure places no theoretical limit on the total rotation or strain experienced by an element.' Cited line in-span. (Source has minor typo 'NLGEOM,ON), activates large-strain effects supported element types' — readable, not a defect.)

dFacts.statement: The total load should be broken into smaller steps because strain increments must be restricted to maintain accuracy in the large-strain procedure.
dFacts.note: Cited line 13050 is the no-theoretical-limit sentence. True support at lines 13052-13053: 'The procedure requires that strain increments be restricted to maintain accuracy, however, so the total load should be broken into smaller steps.'

dFacts.statement: In large-strain solutions, all stress-strain input and results are in terms of true stress and true (or logarithmic) strain.
dFacts.note: Lines 13055-13056 verbatim: 'In large-strain solutions, all stress-strain input and results are in terms of true stress and true (or logarithmic) strain.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: Large Deflections with Small Strain is available in all beam and most shell elements; issue NLGEOM,ON to activate large-deflection effects for small-strain analysis element types that support this feature.
dFacts.note: Lines 13064-13067 (8.4.1.1): 'This feature is available in all beam and most shell elements... Issue the NLGEOM,ON command to activate large-deflection effects for those elements that are designed for small strain analysis types that support this feature.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: For most elements, initial stiffness effects are automatically included when large-deformation effects are activated (NLGEOM,ON).
dFacts.note: Cited line 13092 is the initial-stress sentence. True support at lines 13093-13094 verbatim: 'For most elements, initial stiffness effects are automatically included when large-deformation effects are activated (NLGEOM,ON).'

dFacts.statement: A structure can become unstable when a load reaches its buckling value or when nonlinear material becomes unstable; it is more common in slender structures, and the instability could be global (snap-through of a plate) or local (failure of a stiffener).
dFacts.note: Lines 14609-14611 verbatim (8.11 Unstable Structures). Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: Nonlinear stabilization (p. 303) is a tool for dealing with local instabilities as well as global instability and can be used with nearly any other nonlinear technique (such as line search and automatic time-stepping) but not with the arc-length method.
dFacts.note: Lines 14615-14618: 'Nonlinear stabilization (p. 303) / A tool for dealing with local instabilities as well as global instability. You can use it together with nearly any other nonlinear solution technique, such as line search and automatic time-stepping (although not with the arc-length method).' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The arc-length method (p. 308) can simulate the negative slope portion of a load-vs-displacement curve.
dFacts.note: Lines 14619-14621: 'Arc-length method (p. 308) / This method can circumvent global instability... More importantly, it can simulate the negative slope portion of a load-vs.-displacement curve.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The energy dissipation ratio should be between 0 and 1; use a smaller value for local instability and a larger value for global instability, a smaller value for solid elements and a larger value for shell, beam, and link elements.
dFacts.note: Line 14687 verbatim ('The energy dissipation ratio should be between 0 and 1...'); guidance at lines 14695-14699: 'use a smaller value for local instability and a larger value for global instability. The smaller value should be used for solid elements and the larger value should be used for shell, beam, and link elements.' within +30.

dFacts.statement: It is more efficient and accurate in most cases to activate stabilization in a multiframe restart, restarting from the next-to-last converged substep.
dFacts.note: Lines 14825-14826: 'it is more efficient and accurate in most cases to activate stabilization in a multiframe restart'; lines 14827-14829: 'do not restart from the last converged substep. Rather, restart from the next-to-last converged substep...'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: If the stabilization energy is much less than the potential energy (for example, within a 1.0 percent tolerance), the result should be acceptable.
dFacts.note: Lines 14802-14804 verbatim: 'If the stabilization energy... is much less than the potential energy (for example, within a 1.0 percent tolerance), the result should be acceptable...'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The arc-length method (ARCLEN and ARCTRM) is restricted to static analyses with proportional (ramped) loads only; do not use LNSRCH, PRED, adaptive descent (NROPT,,,ON), automatic time-stepping (AUTOTS, DELTIM), or TIMINT when it is active.
dFacts.note: Lines 14869-14870 verbatim ('restricted to static analyses with proportional (ramped) loads only'); lines 14877-14880: 'do not use line search (LNSRCH), the predictor (PRED), adaptive descent (NROPT,,,ON), automatic time-stepping (AUTOTS, DELTIM), or time-integration effects (TIMINT)' within +30. Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: When the arc-length method is active, do not base convergence on displacement (CNVTOL,U); instead use the force criteria (CNVTOL,F).
dFacts.note: Cited line 14878 is the preceding sentence. True support at lines 14879-14880: 'Likewise, do not try to base convergence on displacement (CNVTOL,U); instead, use the force criteria (CNVTOL,F).'

dFacts.statement: If an arc-length solution fails to converge within NEQIT, the program automatically bisects and continues; you can freely switch from Newton-Raphson to arc-length at the start of any load step, but switching from arc-length to Newton-Raphson requires terminating and restarting with ARCLEN,OFF.
dFacts.note: Lines 14881-14884: 'If an arc-length solution fails to converge within the prescribed maximum number of iterations (NEQIT), the program automatically bisects and continues the analysis'; lines 14893-14896: 'You can freely switch from the Newton-Raphson iteration method to the arc-length method at the start of any load step. However, to switch from arc-length to Newton-Raphson iterations, you must terminate the analysis and restart... (ARCLEN,OFF).' Cited line in-span of first clause; second clause within +30.

dFacts.statement: Place an upper limit on the time-step size (DELTIM or NSUBST), especially for complicated models, to ensure all modes and behaviors of interest are accurately included.
dFacts.note: Lines 15194-15196 verbatim (8.12.2.4 Automatic Time-Stepping). Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: Line search (LNSRCH) is useful for enhancing convergence but expensive (especially with plasticity); consider it for force-loaded structures, 'flimsy' structures with increasing stiffness (such as a fishing pole), and oscillatory convergence patterns.
dFacts.note: Lines 15219-15224 verbatim (8.12.2.5 Line Search) including the three bullets (force-loaded, flimsy/fishing pole, oscillatory convergence). Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: The nonlinear stabilization method can be used to solve both locally and globally unstable problems and to overcome convergence for general problems.
dFacts.note: Lines 15226-15228 verbatim (8.12.2.6 Nonlinear Stabilization). Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: The Graphical Solution Tracking (GST) feature displays the computed convergence norms and criteria while the solution is in process; by default GST is ON for interactive sessions and OFF for batch runs, controlled by the /GST command.
dFacts.note: Lines 15185-15189 (8.12.2.3): 'the Graphical Solution Tracking (GST) feature displays the computed convergence norms and criteria while the solution is in process. By default, GST is ON for interactive sessions and OFF for batch runs. Use the /GST command to turn GST on or off.' Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: Issue the NLDIAG,NRRE command to write Newton-Raphson residuals from equilibrium iterations to a file (Jobname.nrxxx), which can be contour-plotted via PLNSOL,NRRE.
dFacts.note: Lines 15119-15121 verbatim: 'Issue the NLDIAG,NRRE command to write the Newton-Raphson residuals from equilibrium iterations to a file (Jobname.nrxxx). You can then contour plot the residual forces via the PLNSOL,NRRE command...'.

dFacts.statement: The NLDIAG,EFLG command identifies elements that violate nonlinear criteria and records them in a file (Jobname.ndxxx).
dFacts.note: Lines 15148-15149 verbatim: 'The NLDIAG,EFLG command identifies elements that violate the above criteria and records them in a file (Jobname.ndxxx).'.

dFacts.statement: In POST1, only one substep can be read in at a time, and the results from that substep should have been written to Jobname.rst.
dFacts.note: Lines 14188-14190 verbatim: 'Remember that in POST1, only one substep can be read in at a time, and that the results from that substep should have been written to Jobname.rst.'

dFacts.statement: Verify from the output file whether the analysis converged at all load steps; if not, you probably do not want to postprocess the results other than to determine why convergence failed.
dFacts.note: Lines 14201-14203 verbatim (8.6.6.1): 'Verify from your output file (Jobname.out) whether or not the analysis converged at all load steps. If not, you probably do not want to postprocess the results, other than to determine why convergence failed.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The nonlinear example (8.14) activates geometric nonlinearity with nlgeom,on and monitors displacement (monitor,1,ntop,uy) and reaction force (monitor,2,nright,fy) with outres,all,all.
dFacts.note: Example heading verified at line 15645 ('8.14. Example: Nonlinear Analysis'); line 15712 'nlgeom,on ! turn on geometric nonlinearity'; lines 15720-15722 'monitor,1,ntop,uy / monitor,2,nright,fy / outres,all,all', all within +30 of cited line.

dFacts.statement: The NLHIST command enables you to monitor results of interest in real time during solution, with data written to Jobname.nlh.
dFacts.note: Lines 8423-8427 verbatim: 'You may also use the NLHIST command to monitor results of interest in real time during solution... The result data are written to a file named Jobname.nlh.'

dFacts.statement: Use the Newton-Raphson option (NROPT) only in a nonlinear analysis; it specifies how often the tangent matrix is updated during solution.
dFacts.note: Lines 1718-1719 verified verbatim, but this is a strict subset of G5 ('NROPT... is used only in a nonlinear analysis and specifies how often the tangent matrix is updated: ...'). No new content.

dFacts.statement: In the TIME option, time acts as a tracking parameter in rate-independent analyses; if TIME is not issued, the program uses the default time value of 1.0 for the first load step and 1.0 + previous time for other load steps.
dFacts.note: Lines 3405-3408 (3.6.1.1): 'In other, rate-independent analyses, time acts as a tracking parameter... if you do not issue the TIME command at all, the program uses the default time value: 1.0 for the first load step, and 1.0 + previous time for other load steps.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: For a nonlinear or transient analysis, specify the number of substeps within a load step via the DELTIM and NSUBST commands; by default the program uses one substep per load step.
dFacts.note: Lines 3416-3419 verbatim (3.6.1.2), including 'By default, the program uses one substep per load step.' Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: In automatic time stepping, the program calculates an optimum time step at the end of each substep based on the response of the structure to the applied loads; in a nonlinear static analysis AUTOTS determines the size of load increments between substeps.
dFacts.note: Lines 3421-3424 verbatim (3.6.1.3): 'The AUTOTS command activates automatic time stepping. In automatic time stepping, the program calculates an optimum time step at the end of each substep, based on the response of the structure or component to the applied loads. When used in a nonlinear static (or steady-state) analysis, AUTOTS determine the size of load increments between substeps.' Cited line is the anchor.

dFacts.statement: KBC,0 indicates ramped loads and KBC,1 indicates stepped loads; the default depends on the discipline and type of analysis.
dFacts.note: Lines 3427-3428 verbatim (3.6.1.4): 'KBC,0 indicates ramped loads, and KBC,1 indicates stepped loads. The default depends on the discipline and type of analysis.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: Table 3.14 lists NEQIT (maximum number of equilibrium iterations per substep), CNVTOL (convergence tolerances), and NCNV (options for terminating analyses) for nonlinear analyses.
dFacts.note: Lines 3582-3594: 'Table 3.14: Nonlinear Analyses Commands' with rows 'Specifies the maximum number of equilibrium iterations per substep / NEQIT', 'Specifies convergence tolerances / CNVTOL', 'Provides options for terminating analyses / NCNV'. Cited line verbatim the table caption.

dFacts.statement: Convergence is assumed when the residual (out-of-balance) is less than a tolerance times a reference value and/or the DOF increment is less than a tolerance times a reference value; the default is out-of-balance convergence checking only.
dFacts.note: Lines 30053-30055 verbatim (14.10.2 Convergence): 'Convergence, therefore, is obtained when the size of the residual (disequilibrium) is less than a tolerance times a reference value and/or when the size of the DOF increment is less than a tolerance times a reference value. The default is to use out-of-balance convergence checking only.'

dFacts.statement: The default out-of-balance reference value Rref is ||{Fa}||; for DOFs with imposed displacement constraints, the default Rref is {Fnr} at those DOFs.
dFacts.note: Lines 30079-30080 verbatim: 'The default out-of-balance reference value Rref is ||{Fa}||. For DOFs with imposed displacement constraints, the default Rref value is {Fnr} at those DOFs.'

dFacts.statement: There are three available norms (CNVTOL NORM): infinite norm, L1 norm, and L2 norm (SRSS); the default is to use the L2 norm.
dFacts.note: Lines 30065-30073: 'There are three available norms (CNVTOL,,,,NORM) to choose from: 1. Infinite norm 2. L1 norm 3. L2 norm... the L2 norm is the square root of the sum of the squares (SRSS)... The default is to use the L2 norm.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The default reference value uref is calculated using the historic infinity norm of incremental displacement.
dFacts.note: Lines 30105-30106 verbatim: 'The default reference value uref is calculated using the historic infinity norm of incremental displacement.'

dFacts.statement: Adaptive descent is used by default for plasticity, contact, stress stiffness with large strain, and nonlinear magnetics unless the line search or arc-length options are on; it is only available with full Newton-Raphson, which is also the default for plasticity, contact, and large strain nonlinearities.
dFacts.note: Lines 30220-30225: adaptive descent nonlinearities 'plasticity, contact, stress stiffness with large strain, and nonlinear magnetics using the scalar potential formulation. Adaptive descent is used by default in these cases unless the line search or arc-length options are on. It is only available with full Newton-Raphson... Full Newton-Raphson is also the default for plasticity, contact and large strain nonlinearities.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The line search option (LNSRCH) improves a Newton-Raphson solution by scaling the solution vector by a line search parameter s where 0.05 < s < 1.0.
dFacts.note: Lines 30227-30228: 'The line search option (accessed with LNSRCH command) attempts to improve a Newton-Raphson solution {du} by scaling the solution vector by a scalar value termed the line search parameter'; line 30235: 's = line search parameter, 0.05 < s < 1.0'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: s (the line search parameter) is automatically determined by minimizing the energy of the system using an iterative scheme based on regula falsi; LSTOL defaults to 0.5; if go > 0.0 no iterations are performed and s is set to 1.0; s is not allowed below 0.05.
dFacts.note: Cited line 30235 is only 's = line search parameter, 0.05 < s < 1.0'. True support at lines 30241-30252: 's is automatically determined by minimizing the energy of the system...'; 30246-30247 'An iterative solution scheme based on regula falsi is used'; 30248-30249 'LSTOL defaults to 0.5'; 30252 'If go > 0.0, no iterations are performed and s is set to 1.0. s is not allowed below 0.05.'

dFacts.statement: The td-21 example uses SHELL281 (et,1,281) for a ring-stiffened cylinder with 2024-T3 Aluminum alloy and external pressure.
dFacts.note: Title line 2: 'Buckling and Post-buckling analysis of a ring-stiffened cylinder with Nonlinear Stabilization'; line 19 'et,1,281' (SHELL281); line 21 'Material Definition for 2024-T3 Alluminum alloy'; line 14 pext=0.24 with sfe pressure loads (68-93). Cited line 17 ('! Element Definition') is inside the supporting block.

dFacts.statement: The td-21 buckling.dat static analysis uses antype,static, nlgeom,on, pred,on, time,1, nsubst,100,10000,10, rescontrol,define,all,1, outres,all,all, and ncnv,2 (do not terminate the program if the solution diverges).
dFacts.note: Cited line 145 is the upgeom imperfection line. True support at lines 151-159 (static block): 'antype,static / nlgeom,on / pred,on / time,1 / nsubst,100,10000,10 / rescontrol,define,all,1 / outres,all,all / ncnv,2 ! Do not terminate the program execution if the solution diverges'. (Line 154's comment 'No prediction occurs' after pred,on is a corpus comment error, not relevant to the claim.)

dFacts.statement: The td-21 example first performs a linear buckling analysis (pstres,on, antype,buckle, lanbopt,,,BCS), then adds imperfections as a tenth of each mode shape (upgeom,0.1,1,i,buckling,rst), then restarts with stabilization (antype,,restart,1,10, stabilize,constant,energy,0.00012).
dFacts.note: Cited line 164 is a blank line. Verified across the file: prestress solve 'pstres,on' line 125; 'antype,buckle' line 132, 'lanbopt,,,BCS' line 134; 'upgeom,0.1,1,i,buckling,rst ! Add imperfections as a tenth of each mode shape' line 144; restart block lines 167-171: 'antype,,restart,1,10 ... stabilize,constant,energy,0.00012 ! Use energy option'. Span 125-172; anchor = line 125 (start of the sequence).

dFacts.statement: The Delamination of a Stiffened Composite Panel example (Ch. 5) performs a static analysis with large deflection effects (NLGEOM) and a constant stabilization energy dissipation ratio of 0.1 (STABILIZE) to achieve convergence.
dFacts.note: Lines 5761-5763 (section 5.6, example titled 'Delamination of a Stiffened Composite Panel Under a Compressive Load' per page footer 5774): 'A static analysis is performed. Large deflection effects are included (NLGEOM). To achieve a converged solution with this unstable problem, a constant stabilization energy dissipation ratio equal to 0.1 is included (STABILIZE).' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The delamination example shows the level of stabilization energy (STEN) is low compared to the total strain energy (SENE).
dFacts.note: Lines 5766-5768: 'As shown in Figure 5.8: Time History Plot of Strain and Stabilization Energies, the level of stabilization energy (STEN) is low compared to the total strain energy (SENE) throughout the simulation'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: The wind turbine blade example (Ch. 23) demonstrates using beam elements to simulate the behavior of a slender composite structure such as a wind turbine blade.
dFacts.note: Lines 15457-15460: 'Chapter 23: Modal Analysis of a Wind Turbine Blade Using Beam Elements / This example problem demonstrates how to use beam elements to simulate the behavior of a slender composite structure such as a wind turbine blade.' Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: For slender composite structures, use current-technology beam elements (such as BEAM188), verify slenderness ratio and material orientation, use the meshed beam-section subtype (SECTYPE,,BEAM,MESH) and/or tapered-beam section (SECTYPE,,TAPER), select higher-order interpolation in BEAM188 if nonuniform deformation is expected, and use the nonaveraged results file format.
dFacts.note: Lines 15703-15714 (23.8 Recommendations) contain all four bullets: BEAM188 + slenderness ratio/material orientation (15706-15708); SECTYPE,,BEAM,MESH and SECTYPE,,TAPER (15709-15710); higher-order interpolation in BEAM188 (15711-15712); nonaveraged results file format (15714). Cited line is the first bullet.

dFacts.statement: The Bolt Thread Simulation example (Ch. 39) sets the analysis type to static (antype,static) and includes geometric nonlinearity (nlgeom,on).
dFacts.note: Lines 20347-20351 (39.6 Analysis and Solution Controls, 'Bolt Thread Simulation' per page header 20335): 'A nonlinear static analysis is performed in two load steps. Large-deflection effects (NLGEOM) are included in the analysis. / antype,static !selecting analysis / nlgeom,on !including geometric nonlinearity'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: Use the SOLOPTION command to activate the automatic transition from a static to a transient solution (SOLOPTION, Option, Type, Value), with STOT/TTOS options.
dFacts.note: Lines 1835-1839 (3.1 Solution Transition Procedure) verbatim: 'Use the SOLOPTION command to activate the automatic transition from a static to a transient solution: SOLOPTION, Option, Type, Value ... STOT ... TTOS ...'. Cited line is the span start.

dFacts.statement: The SOLOPTION example involves snap-through of a slender beam under pressure where a static solution has difficulty converging; only two SOLOPTION commands (soloption and soloption,ttos,time,0.1) are needed beyond typical input.
dFacts.note: Lines 1850-1860: 'The analysis involves snap-through of a slender beam under pressure' (1851); 'A static solution will have difficulty converging for this model at the point of snap-through' (1853); 'Only two SOLOPTION commands are needed beyond the typical input:' (1856-1857); 'soloption / soloption,ttos,time,0.1' (1859-1860). Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: When using SOLOPTION (mass matrix and algorithmic damping), it is important to define density for all materials; the default backward Euler time integration (SOLOPTION,STOT,,QUASI) is recommended.
dFacts.note: Lines 1929-1931: 'Since the procedure relies on the mass matrix and algorithmic damping to achieve convergence... it is important to define density for all materials when using this method'; lines 1936-1938: 'During the transient solution phase, the default backward Euler time integration (SOLOPTION,STOT,,QUASI) is recommended...'. Cited line in-span.

dFacts.statement: During the transient solution phase, monitor the kinetic energy to potential energy ratio; the kinetic and damping energies should be a very small percentage (<1%) of the potential energy to achieve an accurate solution.
dFacts.note: Lines 1939-1943: 'Monitor the kinetic energy to potential energy ratio during the transient solution to make sure it is close to a static solution... The kinetic and damping energies are representative of the solution approximations made to achieve convergence and should be a very small percentage (<1%) of the potential energy to achieve an accurate solution.' Cited line in-span.

excludedFromDenominator.detail: NROPT,AUTO (program choose, default) and NROPT,FULL (full Newton-Raphson) are exactly the 'Program-chosen (default)' and 'Full' options already enumerated in G5 (SAG line 1718); verified at CR 53389-53393 but no new content.
NROPT,MODI = modified Newton-Raphson and NROPT,INIT = initial-stiffness matrix match G5's enumerated 'Modified' and 'Initial stiffness' options; verified at CR 53399-53402 but no new content.

NROPT,UNSYM = full Newton-Raphson with unsymmetric matrices matches G5's enumerated 'Full with unsymmetric matrix' option; true text at CR 53403-53405, cited line 53402 is the INIT entry; no material new content.
'NEQIT specifies the maximum number of equilibrium iterations' is verbatim the NEQIT clause of G3 (SAG line 1672); verified at CR 51241 but no new content.
'CNVTOL sets convergence values for nonlinear analyses' (CR 17608, verbatim) is the same claim as G4's 'CNVTOL sets the convergence criteria'; no new content.
'CUTCONTROL controls time-step cutback during a nonlinear solution' (CR 19446, verbatim) is the same claim as G4's 'CUTCONTROL controls bisections (cutback criteria)'; no new content.
SAG 1718-1719 verified verbatim, but it is a strict subset of G5 (NROPT nonlinear-only + tangent-matrix update frequency); no new content.
